title: arXiv mathematics — 27 October 2026: 9 notable papers on conjecture resolutions, sharp bounds, and cross-field methods
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart, so this is an inferred ordering of notable papers—not measured popularity—and citation evidence is limited for this very recent batch. Semantic Scholar records returned no citation-count or influential-citation fields for these selected IDs, so citation momentum could not be measured.

sections.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
sections.abstract: The authors claim that no Lee ball of radius r≥2 tiles ℤⁿ by translations when n≥3, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that for every n≥3 and r≥2, ℤⁿ cannot be tiled by translates of the Lee ball Bₙ(r), without assuming the set of centres is linear, periodic, or has a density.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Integer lattice ℤⁿ with Lee distance; translational tilings by one fixed Lee ball and all centre sets, for n≥3 and r≥2.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that the existence classification does not classify the individual perfect Lee codes in the remaining admissible cases (n≤2 or r=1).
sections.ranking_evidence: The introduction states the unrestricted-centre theorem and its scope explicitly; the result is also surfaced in MathWorld’s Golomb–Welch entry, providing an independent secondary pointer to the claimed resolution.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
themes: Functional analysis & operator algebras (added theme; no controlled theme precisely fits)
sections.abstract: The authors prove that lower semi-continuity of a C*-algebra weight and normality of a von Neumann algebra weight can each be detected on the corresponding commutative subalgebras.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show that a weight is lower semi-continuous if its restrictions to commutative C*-subalgebras are lower semi-continuous, and derive the von Neumann algebra counterpart: normality follows from normality on commutative von Neumann subalgebras.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Weights on C*-algebras and von Neumann algebras; the commutative tests involve the relevant positive sums, and normality is understood as preserving directed suprema.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors disclose that the proofs were substantially obtained with GPT-6.0 and then checked and rewritten by the authors; this report has not independently verified the proofs.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper states an affirmative answer to Haagerup’s 1975 Problem 1.11 and provides explicit equivalences in two operator-algebra settings; the result was also independently indexed by Wolfram MathWorld.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: The C_p conjecture of Muckenhoupt
sections.abstract: For 1<p<∞, the authors claim that the C_p weight condition is necessary and sufficient for weighted inequalities relating the Hilbert transform to the Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator and for the weighted Fefferman–Stein inequality.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the sparse estimate needed to establish sufficiency of C_p, completing the asserted necessary-and-sufficient characterization for both inequalities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Weights w on ℝ satisfying the stated C_p condition with parameters r>1 and K<∞; the result is stated for 1<p<∞, with the authors saying the argument extends to ℝⁿ.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s p-range excludes the endpoints p=1 and p=∞; the paper’s main exposition is one-dimensional and points to a remark for the higher-dimensional extension.
sections.ranking_evidence: The introduction identifies this as the resolution of Muckenhoupt’s long-standing sufficiency conjecture and gives a concrete sparse-operator estimate from which the weighted theorem follows.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
sections.abstract: The author proves the remaining sharp D-edge-coloring bounds for planar graphs with maximum degree Δ≥6, completing the conjectured bound after earlier work handled Δ≤5 and Δ≥33.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves a D-coloring with 2Δ−1 colors for every planar graph of maximum degree Δ≥6; Δ=6 is computer-assisted.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A D-coloring is a proper edge coloring in which every K₄ minus an edge subgraph is rainbow; Wang’s conjectured counts for Δ=4 and 5 were established earlier, while this paper settles Δ≥6.
sections.unique_caveat: The Δ=6 case depends on computer-assisted certificates; reproducing and independently checking the ancillary verification is an important review step.
sections.ranking_evidence: This closes the parameter gap left by the earlier Δ≤5 and Δ≥33 cases; the arXiv record says the Δ=6 case comes with ancillary certificates and verification scripts, making the computational part checkable.
sections.comment: 21 pages; ancillary files contain certificates and verification scripts for the computer-assisted case of maximum degree 6
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erdős--Nicolas--Sárközy Conjecture
sections.abstract: For admissible subsets of {1,…,N}, the authors prove that their count grows as exp(Θ(√N)), as conjectured by Erdős, Nicolas, and Sárközy.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove exp(c√N)≤a(N)≤exp(C√N) for absolute c,C>0 and every N≥4, with the same order for admissible sets whose maximum is N.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite set is admissible when any two of its subsets with equal sum have equal cardinality; a(N) counts nonempty admissible subsets of {1,…,N}.
sections.unique_caveat: The result fixes the order of growth but not a leading constant or finer asymptotic for log a(N); the upper bound uses a proportional-size subset with controlled doubling.
sections.ranking_evidence: The preprint gives matching exponential-order upper and lower bounds and a concrete additive-combinatorial ingredient for the upper bound; the result also appears in MathDB’s conjecture listing.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
sections.abstract: The authors extend a dynamical form of the prime number theorem to multivariate polynomials of sufficiently large Birch rank and establish analogous averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the stated dynamical Chowla-type conclusions for multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large relative to degree, plus analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Multivariate polynomials subject to a degree-dependent lower bound on Birch rank; the abstract does not state the numerical threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not cover all multivariate polynomials: low Birch-rank cases are outside the stated hypothesis.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work bridges number theory, algebraic geometry, and dynamics, extending the prior Bergelson–Richter result to a genuinely multivariate regime; the exact rank condition makes the scope checkable in the abstract.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
sections.abstract: The author proves spectral-edge convergence of suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations of general Wigner matrices to the stochastic Airy operator and gives sharp couplings for several classical ensembles.
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes convergence to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition for the Wigner setting and sharp couplings for Gaussian, Laguerre, and circular β-ensembles, respectively.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations formed from deterministic initial vectors; the abstract describes general Wigner matrices, while the exact entry-distribution and moment hypotheses are specified in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: “General Wigner” is not assumption-free; the abstract alone does not give the precise entry and moment conditions needed to apply the theorem.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper links random-matrix edge statistics to operator limits, with additional joint eigenvalue, eigenfunction, and spectral-measure convergence; it also reports quantitative coupling errors for Airy, Bessel, and Sine operators.
sections.journal_reference: Not available from the sources checked

sections.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
sections.abstract: The author modifies the Cohn–Elkies linear program using constraints on short lattice vectors to improve lattice-packing upper bounds in specified dimension ranges.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves a certified upper bound based on a modified linear program that exploits restrictions on how short vectors can co-occur in classes modulo 2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full-rank Euclidean lattices normalized to have shortest nonzero vector of length 1; the result bounds lattice packing density, not arbitrary sphere packings.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports upper-bound improvements, not new dense lattice constructions; the margin over the comparison bounds diminishes in some higher dimensions.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper reports improvement over the three-point bound for dimensions 11–16 and below published numerical Cohn–Elkies values across several further ranges; it supplies exact rational certificates and verification code.
sections.comment: Links to a GitHub repository with relevant numerical data

sections.title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
sections.abstract: The authors characterize Pareto-optimal variance–sensitivity tradeoffs for unbiased estimators via Hellinger–Kantorovich geometry and give a Z-estimation method that attains such pairs asymptotically.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that the model’s Hellinger–Kantorovich geometry determines the full Pareto front and that their Z-estimation procedure asymptotically achieves optimal pairs; in the stated asymptotic sense, maximum likelihood has the least sensitivity among estimators with optimal variance.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unbiased estimators in a given statistical model; the Pareto characterization is asymptotic where relevant, and applied construction requires solving a continuum of PDEs.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors execute the full PDE-based program only for selected nontrivial parametric examples, so practical construction in general models remains unresolved.
sections.ranking_evidence: A four-category bridge connects statistical decision tradeoffs to a geometry interpolating Hellinger and Wasserstein structures; the abstract gives both an asymptotic construction and a concrete maximum-likelihood consequence.
